title: Template CLI: `init` scaffolder + `doctor` environment validator
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Build a small CLI that (1) scaffolds a chosen Quickstart Template into a local directory and (2) validates that the developer’s machine/env is correctly configured to run it (API key present, model configured, OTel collector reachable).

Context
We’re shipping production-minded RAG + agent templates (Python + TypeScript first). Early internal beta feedback shows the biggest onboarding failures are configuration mistakes (missing key/model), and "it runs but I see nothing in Console" issues (OTel exporter misconfigured / collector not reachable).

Scope
1) `init` command
- Scaffolds template into a target directory with a consistent folder layout and README.
- Writes a template version stamp so support/docs can correlate issues.
- Does NOT write secrets into files by default.

2) `doctor` command
- Validates required env vars (API key, model, base URL) and prints actionable remediation.
- Verifies basic API connectivity with a minimal request.
- Verifies OTel collector/exporter settings (best-effort) and provides clear next steps.

Non-goals (v1)
- In-place template upgrades/migrations ("upgrade" command) beyond printing what version you’re on.
- Auto-deploy (Fly/Render/k8s) from the CLI.
- Managing API keys (creating/rotating) — only validates presence/format and connectivity.

Proposed CLI UX
Binary name: `redwood-quickstart` (subject to packaging constraints; if npm-only, use `npx redwood-quickstart@<ver> ...`).

Commands:
- `redwood-quickstart init`
  - Interactive prompt if no args: select template (python-rag-agent, ts-rag-agent)
  - Flags:
    - `--template <id>`
    - `--dir <path>` (default: current dir)
    - `--no-telemetry-tags` (default: telemetry tagging off unless explicitly enabled)
    - `--overwrite` (guarded; requires confirmation)
  - Output:
    - Creates template directory/files
    - Writes `.redwood-template.json` (or `.redwood-template-version`) with: template id + version + created_at
    - Leaves `.env` untouched; ships `.env.example` only

- `redwood-quickstart doctor`
  - Checks:
    - Env vars present: `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_MODEL` (or template-specific model var), optional `REDWOOD_BASE_URL`
    - Configuration sanity: max token / timeout defaults present (per PM-914), warns if missing
    - Connectivity: performs a lightweight API call (e.g., list models or small chat completion) and reports HTTP status, request id if present
    - OTel: validates exporter env vars if set (e.g., `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`), attempts a short export of a test span OR checks collector health endpoint if known; prints link to local docker-compose instructions if unreachable
    - Telemetry tags: warns if enabled and likely to be blocked by corporate proxy; recommends opt-in only
  - Exit codes:
    - 0: OK
    - 10: missing required env
    - 11: auth failure
    - 12: connectivity failure
    - 13: otel exporter/collector failure (non-fatal if user opts out of observability)

Implementation notes
- Keep implementation dependency-light and cross-platform (macOS/Linux; Windows best-effort).
- Ensure no secrets are logged. `doctor` output must redact keys (show last 4 only).
- `doctor` should surface Redwood request id if available to help support triage.
- Avoid high-cardinality tags in any test spans/metrics. Any test span should use fixed attributes only.
- Template version stamp should be included in `doctor` output so support can ask for it.

Success criteria
- Reduced support tickets for "missing key/model" and "collector not receiving traces" during internal beta and first public release.
- Internal dogfood: new engineer can run `init` + `doctor` and be running the template (including seeing a trace) in < 10 minutes.

References
- ADR: decide to ship a minimal CLI + GitHub templates (CLI is optional, templates remain runnable without it)
- Observability conventions: required attributes + redaction rules
- Safe defaults policy: timeouts/retries/cost caps to warn about in `doctor`
acceptance_criteria: `init` scaffolds python and typescript RAG+agent templates with a consistent README and `.env.example`
`init` writes a version stamp file and prints it at the end of scaffolding
`init` never writes secrets and never echoes full API keys to stdout
`doctor` fails fast with clear messages when `REDWOOD_API_KEY` or model config is missing
`doctor` validates API connectivity and prints HTTP status plus Redwood request id (if present)
`doctor` validates OTel exporter/collector reachability (best-effort) and provides a deterministic next step when it can’t validate
All output follows redaction rules and does not introduce high-cardinality attributes
Docs/README includes how to run `doctor` and interpret common failures
implementation_plan: Define CLI package name + distribution mechanism (npm-first; keep a wrapper script in repo for local dev)
Implement `init`: template registry, prompt flow, file copy, overwrite guard, version stamp writing
Implement `doctor`: env validation + API connectivity check + request id capture
Implement `doctor`: OTel checks (endpoint parse/validation + optional health check + minimal test export behind flag)
Add basic CLI tests (golden snapshot of `init` file tree; `doctor` unit tests for env validation)
Run security review pass: ensure logs redact keys and no secrets are written
open_questions: Packaging: do we want `npx`-only v1 or also a standalone binary later (Go/Rust)?
OTel validation approach: do we attempt a real OTLP export by default, or only validate configuration + optionally export with `--emit-test-span`?
Template telemetry tags: keep default off and require explicit `--enable-telemetry-tags` to avoid proxy/header issues?
progress_updates: 2025-02-10 (Monica): Drafted CLI UX + exit codes; aligned with Elliot on README touch points.
2025-02-13 (Allison): Requested OTel checks avoid test span attributes beyond fixed keys; no dynamic IDs in span attributes.
2025-02-17 (Christine): Asked that `doctor` connectivity check use a very small request and strict timeout to avoid hanging behind proxies.
2025-02-20 (Monica): `init` implementation ready; includes `.redwood-template-version` stamp and `.env.example` only.
2025-02-24 (Monica): `doctor` implemented with env validation + API ping; OTel check is best-effort and non-fatal unless `--require-otel` is passed.
2025-03-01 (Monica): Merged; follow-up created to consider `upgrade` command after public launch feedback.
comments: 2025-02-12 Allison Grant: Please ensure any "test span" uses fixed attributes only (no user machine name, no directory path). Also avoid exporting metrics from doctor; spans only if needed.
2025-02-12 Ibrahim Khan: For API ping, prefer an endpoint that doesn’t burn tokens (models list) if available; otherwise cap to minimal tokens and set a hard timeout.
2025-02-18 Marcus Lin: Confirmed: don’t create `.env` automatically. `.env.example` is fine. Doctor output must redact `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (last 4).
2025-02-23 Dana Lo: TS template init should preserve `package-lock`/`pnpm-lock` behavior; please don’t rewrite lockfiles during scaffold.
2025-02-26 Priya Shah: Please include exit codes in docs. Support wants to ask users to paste `doctor` output (with key redacted).
